evidence: Cic. Ac. 1.19: quid vērum, quid falsum, quid rēctum in ōrātiōne prāvumve
terms.comment: The opposite is prāvus (Traupman 28). Latin often uses the adverb: rēctē respondistī, that’s the right answer; rēctē scrībere, to spell correctly (Traupman 29). Of a statement, true: see true.

evidence: Quint. 1.5.1: ut ēmendāta, ut dīlūcida, ut ōrnāta sit
terms.comment: Of speech, writing or reading: corrected, and so without a mistake; the adverb is ēmendātē (Traupman 29).

evidence: Traupman 29: rēctē loquī (scrībere), to speak (spell) correctly

phrases.latin: certa sit ergō in prīmīs lēctiō, deinde conjūncta et diū lentior, dōnec exercitātiōne contingat ēmendāta vēlōcitās
phrases.english: let reading first be sure, then joined up, and for a long time rather slow, until practice brings speed without mistakes
Did I spell it right? — Yes, you did.
